title: Word 2 — On Holy Baptism
attribution_note: Word 2 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: The promise of salvation in Christ's words

pairs.en: Our Lord and Savior spoke this word for our strengthening and comfort: *“Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved.”* What could be more comforting to a faithful and baptized soul than these words, which promise it eternal salvation?

Beloved Christians! Glory be to God—we believe the Gospel and have been enlightened by holy Baptism. But let us consider the power of holy Baptism, and look at what we were before Baptism and what we became after Baptism, that from this too we may draw living comfort.
Through holy Baptism we were delivered from great calamity and received all true blessedness by the grace of God.
Before Baptism we were far from God, but through Baptism we drew near to God.
Before Baptism we were enemies of God, but by Baptism we were reconciled to God, and God was reconciled to us.

sections.heading: From wrath and darkness to mercy and light

pairs.en: Before Baptism we were children of the wrath of God, but after Baptism we became vessels of the mercy of God.
Before Baptism we were children of darkness and children of the devil, but having been baptized, we became children of light and children of God.
Before Baptism we were defiled by sins, but by Baptism we *“were washed, were sanctified, were justified”* [1 Corinthians 6:11].
Before Baptism we were lost, but having been baptized, we became saved.
Before Baptism the doors to eternal life and the heavenly kingdom were closed to us, but by Baptism they were opened, and those who keep the grace of holy Baptism enter there without hindrance.

sections.heading: A gift of grace, purchased by Christ's blood

pairs.en: These and other benefits of God we receive through holy Baptism, and we receive them as a gift, without any merit of our own, by God's love for mankind alone. For what can one who is lost deserve? Glory to the goodness of God, glory to His love for mankind, glory to His mercy, glory to His bounty! *Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and forevermore!* All this most exalted mercy of God was earned for us by the Only-Begotten Son of God, Jesus Christ our Savior, earned by His precious Blood and His death.

Beloved Christians! Let us remember holy Baptism and examine ourselves, whether we live worthily of holy Baptism, lest this very Baptism become for us the greater condemnation on the day of Christ's dread Judgment, where every lawless word, deed, and thought is judged. Amen.
